articles.title: Stock Futures Churn in Run-Up to Micron Earnings: Markets Wrap
articles.summary: US stocks ticked higher as investors looked ahead to Micron Technology Inc.’s results for the next read on whether artificial intelligence spending is living up to expectations.

articles.title: SK Hynix Seeks $29 Billion With US Listing to Fund AI Boom
articles.summary: SK Hynix Inc. is planning to raise 45.45 trillion won ($29.4 billion) in a landmark US listing, as companies along the artificial intelligence supply chain rush to increase capacity to meet memory chip demand.

articles.title: The Debasement Trade Is Unraveling and Kevin Warsh Is One Big Reason
articles.summary: In hindsight, the beginning of the end for the debasement trade can be traced back to Jan. 30.

articles.title: Stock Rout Pauses, Europe Heat Wave Intensifies | The Pulse 6/24/2026
articles.summary:
"The Pulse With Francine Lacqua" is all about conversations with high profile guests in the beating heart of global business, economics, finance and politics. Based in London, we go wherever the story is, bringing you exclusive interviews and market-moving scoops.

Today's guests: Joyce Chang, JPMorgan Global Research Chair; Clemens Fuest, Ifo Institute President; Miljan Gutovic, Holcim CEO; Benoit Bazin, Saint-Gobain CEO.    (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Investor Who Scored 900% Win in 2008 Crisis Has New Big Short Bet
articles.summary: Hedge fund manager Lee Robinson notched a 900% gain during the global financial crisis by turning a $20 million position into $200 million with timely bets against the US subprime mortgage sector.

articles.title: Options Trades Highlight Doubts Over Prospect of US Rate Hikes
articles.summary: Options traders are building up bets that the broader market overreacted to the Federal Reserve’s hawkish pivot when it priced in a series of interest-rate hikes in the US starting later this year.

articles.title: Airbus A380 Aircraft Require Checks for Possible Wing Cracks
articles.summary: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency is asking some operators of Airbus SE A380 jets to perform additional inspections on their aircraft’s wings after identifying possible cracks in the structure.

articles.title: Rheinmetall Sinks as Germany Shelves Major Warship Contract
articles.summary: Rheinmetall AG shares plunged Wednesday as Germany withdrew from a key warships contract, dealing a blow to investor confidence in the defense contractor following years of huge gains.

articles.title: US Exceptionalism Nearing Expiration Date, HSBC’s Kettner Says
articles.summary: Max Kettner, chief multi-asset strategist at HSBC, says investors may want to be “perhaps really leaning a bit more into that European story,” as he sees an August expiration date on US exceptionalism. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Europe Heat Wave Strains Power Supply, Sends Prices Soaring
articles.summary: Europe’s electricity system is under mounting pressure from an intense heat wave, with extreme swings in power prices as soaring temperatures drive up demand and curb output.

articles.title: Investors Maxing Out AI Trade Feed Stock Market Volatility
articles.summary: Investors are maxing out the AI trade, setting the stock market up for a volatile summer.

articles.title: Gold Drops to Near $4,000 on Stronger Dollar, Fed Rate Outlook
articles.summary: Gold fell for a second day, extending losses to trade near $4,000 an ounce as a stronger US dollar continues to put pressure on prices.

articles.title: US Diesel Prices Fall Under $5, Easing Inflationary Pressure
articles.summary: The cost of diesel in the US fell below $5 a gallon for the first time since mid-March, offering some relief for one of the global economy’s most important fuels.

articles.title: EU Competition Chief Warns Governments Not to Stymie Bank Deals
articles.summary: The European Union’s competition chief has warned nations against overusing tactics such as citing security risks to stymie bank deals needed to boost the economy.

articles.title: South Korea Delays Single-Stock Weekly Options Days Before Start
articles.summary: South Korea has delayed a plan to launch weekly single-stock options on shares including SK Hynix Inc. and Samsung Electronics Co., the latest sign regulators are becoming jittery after wild stock-market swings.

articles.title: Oil Extends Drop as More Tankers Cross Hormuz After Peace Talks
articles.summary: Oil extended declines as more tankers openly cross the Strait of Hormuz, while the US and Iran signal progress toward ending the war.

articles.title: Indonesia Tightens Oversight of Financial Influencers
articles.summary: Indonesia is requiring financial influencers to disclose paid promotions and obtain licenses to recommend assets as Southeast Asia’s largest economy joins a global movement to tighten oversight of the social media personalities.

articles.title: Indian Bonds Rally as RBI Governor Says Rate Hike Talk Premature
articles.summary: India’s benchmark bond yields and swap rates fell to their lowest levels in three months as the nation’s central bank Governor pushed back against expectations for tighter monetary policy.

articles.title: Indian State Lenders Said to Seek $2 Billion in Overseas Loans
articles.summary: Some Indian state-run financial institutions are planning to raise overseas loans of as much as $2 billion using a central bank facility for borrowing at concessional rates, according to people familiar with the matter.

articles.title: Korea’s Surging Equity Volatility Draws Meme-Stock Comparisons
articles.summary: The volatility in South Korea’s benchmark equity index has become so extreme that investors and analysts are likening the market’s surging intra-day swings to the meme-stock frenzy.
